title: Why You're Taller in the Morning Than at Night
seo_title: Why You're Taller in the Morning
meta_description: Most people are about a centimeter taller in the morning than at night. Here's the simple, harmless reason your spine compresses a little through the day.
excerpt: Your height quietly changes between morning and night — and the harmless reason is hiding in your spine.

content_html:
Measure your height first thing tomorrow morning, then again right before bed. For most people the evening number is up to about a centimeter shorter, and it happens to nearly everyone. The reason is a simple, harmless thing your spine does every single day.

It is not shrinking in any worrying way, and it is not in your head. It is just gravity and a bit of clever cushioning at work.

Your spine has built-in shock absorbers

Between each of the bones in your spine sits a soft disc, a bit like a small water-filled cushion. These discs let your back bend, twist, and soak up the jolts of walking, lifting, and sitting. They are mostly water.

All day, while you are upright, gravity gently presses down through your spine. That steady pressure squeezes a little fluid out of each disc, so every disc gets slightly thinner. Stack that tiny loss across all the discs in your back and neck, and you end the day a touch shorter.

Overnight, the discs soak the water back up

When you lie down to sleep, the downward pressure comes off your spine. The discs slowly draw fluid back in and plump up again, like sponges expanding once you stop squeezing them. By morning you are back to your full height.

That is why you are tallest soon after waking, and why a height reading at the doctor can come out a hair different depending on the time of day.

Why some days the difference feels bigger

A few ordinary things can make the daily dip more noticeable:

  • A long day on your feet, or many hours sitting upright.
  • Heavy lifting or a tough workout that loads the spine.
  • Getting older, since discs tend to hold a little less water over the years, which is a normal part of aging.

None of this is something you need to fix. It is simply your spine doing its job and resetting overnight.

A fun extreme: astronauts

Take gravity away entirely and the effect gets dramatic. In space, with nothing pressing the discs down, astronauts can temporarily gain a few centimeters of height, then settle back to normal once they are home and gravity goes back to work.

When it is worth a quick check

Day-to-day height change is completely normal and nothing to watch. If you ever notice your height steadily dropping over months or years, or you have ongoing back discomfort, it is a reasonable thing to mention to a doctor at a routine visit, so a professional can take a calm look. For the everyday morning-to-night difference, there is nothing to do at all.

The bottom line

You really are a little taller in the morning than at night, and it comes down to soft spinal discs squeezing out a bit of water under gravity through the day and soaking it back up while you sleep. If this surprised you, the way a full night's sleep quietly resets the body is worth a look too.
